subject: common-workplace-fundamentals
summary: Explains the structure of HTTP requests and responses, HTTP methods, and how to interpret status codes to diagnose API errors.
key_points: HTTP requests consist of a request line, headers, and an optional body.
Status codes indicate error ownership: 4xx is client-side, 5xx is server-side.
Always check both the status code and the response body to diagnose errors.
misconceptions: A 5xx error can be fixed by changing the client request.
GET requests can reliably include a request body.
check_questions: What are the three main parts of an HTTP request?
What is the difference between status codes 401 and 403?
If you receive a 5xx error, whose side has the problem?

fact_candidates: HTTP method purposes (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
Status code categories and their meanings (2xx, 4xx, 5xx)
practical_judgment_candidates: Determining error ownership from a status code
Choosing the correct HTTP method for a given operation
error_interpretation_candidates: Reading a 422 validation error response to identify the failing field
Distinguishing 401 from 403 in an authentication flow
scenario_candidates: User registration returning 422 due to short password
GET request returning 401 because of missing auth token
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Attempting to fix a 500 error by modifying the client request
